summary: Root cause is NOT the payment-service v6.0.0 release. The shared ledger-db (Postgres) filled its data volume: disk_used_pct climbed steadily from 78.6% at 11:00 (before any deploy) to 100% at ~15:00, coincident with WARN logs about an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining 33–93 GB of WAL since 12:19. Once the volume hit 100%, ledger-db could no longer extend files, so ALL writers to it failed with "No space left on device" at 15:00–15:01 — payment-service (ledger writes) AND order-service (orders) simultaneously. payment-service's spike to 60-70% error rate is collateral damage from its shared datastore. The v6.0.0 deploy (14:46) and its rollback (15:12) are red herrings: disk was already at 97.9% before the deploy, bank_api_error_rate is flat, and error rate stayed at ~62% for 1h45m after the rollback. This matches HIST-114 exactly. category=resource_exhaustion, root_cause_service=ledger-db.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db disk exhaustion from inactive replication slot retaining WAL
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db's data volume (shared Postgres) filled with WAL retained by the inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' from ~12:19 onward. Disk reached 100% at ~15:00, and Postgres could no longer extend files, so all writers failed with 'No space left on device' — including payment-service ledger writes and order-service order inserts. payment-service v6.0.0 is a coincidental red herring.

causal_chain.claim: Replication slot 'analytics_cdc' goes inactive ~12:19, retaining tens of GB of WAL
Disk at 100% -> Postgres cannot extend files / write WAL
All shared-datastore writers fail: payment-service ledger writes and order-service inserts at ~15:00
payment-service error rate spikes to 60-70% and stays high after rollback

assumptions: Disk growth was driven predominantly by retained WAL (slot messages are frequent but quantify MB, not GB; not proven to be the sole consumer).

ranked_hypotheses.title: payment-service v6.0.0 mandate flow broke ledger writes
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The new mandate flow / MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry type in v6.0.0 caused ledger write failures that propagate to a 60% payment error rate.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Disk was already 97.9% at 14:30 before the 14:46 deploy; order-service (no deploy) failed identically at 15:00:42; rolling back v6.0.0 at 15:12 left error rate at ~62% for 1h45m. The error is a disk-space error, not a mandate/entry-type validation error.

ranked_hypotheses.title: bank-partner-api (external dependency) degradation
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The external bank partner API degraded/unavailable, causing payment failures.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: bank_api_error_rate is flat at ~0.20% throughout; errors reference ledger file extension, not bank calls; order-service is unaffected by any bank dependency yet failed.

ranked_hypotheses.title: ledger-db connection pool exhaustion
ranked_hypotheses.statement: ledger-db ran out of available connections, blocking writes.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: connections_active stayed flat (~62 avg) and the failing error is explicitly 'No space left on device', not a pool/timeout error.

facts.statement: payment-service error rate jumped from ~0.2% to 60-70% starting in the 14:54 bucket and stayed elevated through the end of data.
payment-service ledger writes failed with 'could not extend file: No space left on device' from 15:00:26.
ledger-db disk_used_pct rose from 78.63% (11:00) to 100% (15:00) and stayed at 100%; already 97.9% at 14:30, before the deploy.
ledger-db logged an inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' retaining 33–93 GB of WAL from 12:19, and hit disk-usage 90/95/98% warnings before PANIC 'No space left on device' at 15:01.
order-service, which has no deploy and only shares ledger-db, also failed with 'No space left on device' from 15:00:42.
The only deployment was dep-6203 payment-service v6.0.0 at 14:46, rolled back at 15:12; ledger-db had no deployments, and there were no config changes.
payment-service bank_api_error_rate stayed flat ~0.20% and request_rate ~100 req/s.
ledger-db replication_lag_ms climbed from ~0.9s to ~5.2s over the window.
ledger-db is a shared Postgres used by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
Historical incident HIST-114 had the same symptom and root cause (inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled).

assumptions: The inactive replication slot 'analytics_cdc' (and its retained WAL) is the primary consumer of the ledger-db volume; the slot messages quantify retained MB but the exact GB share of total disk use is not directly shown.
The huge per-message 'retaining <N> MB' values are WAL retained by that slot, consistent with the disk growth trend.

timeline.event: ledger-db disk_used_pct already 78.63% and rising (pre-incident baseline drift).
First WARN: replication slot 'analytics_cdc' inactive, retaining 63157 MB of WAL.
ledger-db disk 97.9% — before the payment-service deploy.
dep-6203 payment-service v6.0.0 (new UPI mandate flow, MANDATE_HOLD ledger entry) deployed.
payment-service error rate bucket spikes to avg 20.22% (max 60.8%).
First payment-service 'ledger write failed: No space left on device'.
First order-service 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device'.
First ledger-db PANIC 'could not write to file pg_wal/xlogtemp...: No space left on device'.
v6.0.0 rolled back — but error rate stays ~62% afterwards.
Latest data: ledger-db still at 100% disk, payment-service error rate still ~62%.

recommended_actions.action: Immediately free space on ledger-db: drop/inactivate the orphaned replication slot 'analytics_cdc' (after confirming the consumer is truly gone) and/or expand the volume, then verify disk drops below 100% and writes resume.
recommended_actions.rationale: Volume is at 100% and all shared-datastore writers (payment-service, order-service) are failing; freeing the retained WAL is the direct remediation.

recommended_actions.action: Re-enable/restore the v6.0.0 deploy if it was rolled back solely on the assumption it caused the outage; the rollback did not fix anything and may have removed an intended feature.
recommended_actions.rationale: Rollback at 15:12 did not change the ~62% error rate; the deploy was not the cause.

recommended_actions.action: Add alerting on ledger-db disk_used_pct (warn >85%, page >92%) and on inactive/behind replication slots (retained WAL), as recommended in HIST-114.
recommended_actions.rationale: Disk was visibly climbing for 4 hours with no page; the same failure mode occurred in HIST-114.

recommended_actions.action: Audit replication slot lifecycle: any slot with no active consumer should be dropped automatically or alerted within minutes.
recommended_actions.rationale: A single inactive slot retained tens of GB of WAL and took down a shared database.

recommended_actions.action: Reduce blast radius by decoupling non-critical services from the highly-shared ledger-db and reviewing volume headroom / autogrowth policies.
recommended_actions.rationale: A shared Postgres amplified a disk issue into a multi-service, SEV-1 outage.

data_gaps: No filesystem-level breakdown (WAL vs tables vs temp files) to quantify exactly how much space the retained 'analytics_cdc' WAL consumed versus other growth; the slot messages report retained MB but not the total.
No ledger-db restart/failover logs or evidence of whether the DB recovered automatically after space was freed (volume still 100% at end of data, so recovery was never reached).
No logs from the slot's intended consumer (e.g. analytics/CDC pipeline) to confirm the slot is genuinely orphaned versus merely lagging.

settlement-service and portfolio-service showed 0 ERRORs in the window, but these are complete (non-truncated) results only within their reported data range; they may write less frequently and simply had no failing writes yet.

findings.statement: payment-service error rate was normal (~0.2%) through 14:45 and jumped to avg 20.22% (max 60.8%) in the 14:54 bucket, then held ~60-70% through the end of data (16:51 last bucket avg 61.47%).
payment-service WARN+ logs from 15:00:26 onward are overwhelmingly ERROR 'ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device' (354 of 358 matches).

refs.quote: ledger write failed: ERROR: could not extend file: No space left on device (payment e3489438)

findings.statement: ledger-db disk_used_pct rose monotonically from 78.63% at 11:00 to 99.39% at 14:45, reached 100.0 at 15:00 and stayed pinned at 100 through 16:45; it was already 97.9% at 14:30, before the 14:46 deploy.

ledger-db logs show repeated WARN 'replication slot \'analytics_cdc\' is inactive; retaining <N> MB of WAL' from 12:19:34 onward, with disk-usage warnings rising 90% (13:10) -> 95% (14:15) -> 98% (14:48), then PANIC/could-not-write errors with 'No space left on device' starting 15:01:01.

refs.quote: replication slot 'analytics_cdc' is inactive; retaining 63157 MB of WAL
PANIC: could not write to file "pg_wal/xlogtemp.37478": No space left on device

findings.statement: order-service — an independent service that only shares ledger-db — shows 236 ERRORs 'INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device', first at 15:00:42, i.e. the same ~15:00 onset as payment-service, despite having no deploy of its own.

refs.quote: INSERT INTO orders failed: No space left on device orderId=8ab6dc3a

findings.statement: Only one deployment exists across all services in the window: dep-6203 payment-service v6.0.0 at 14:46:00 ('New UPI mandate flow', 'new ledger entry type MANDATE_HOLD'), rolled_back at 15:12:00; ledger-db had zero deployments.
Zero config/feature-flag changes across all services in 13:00-16:59.
payment-service bank_api_error_rate was flat at ~0.20% throughout 14:00-16:56, and request_rate stayed ~100 req/s — no upstream bank/partner degradation and no traffic surge.
ledger-db connections_active stayed flat ~54-72 across the whole window; no connection-pool exhaustion.
ledger-db replication_lag_ms rose from ~926ms at 11:00 to ~5.2s at 16:45, consistent with an inactive/falling-behind slot retaining WAL.

Historical incident HIST-114 (2025-04-18, ledger-db) has identical symptoms 'no space left on device' / 'write failures' with root cause 'Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled' (resource_exhaustion).

refs.quote: Inactive replication slot retained WAL until disk filled

findings.statement: payment-service dependency graph: it writes to shared ledger-db and calls bank-partner-api, and its only caller is api-gateway.
ledger-db is shared by order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service.
Error rate remained ~62% for ~1h45m after the 15:12 rollback of v6.0.0, so the rollback did not recover the incident — the faulty change was not in payment-service code.

Because order-service (no deploy) failed at the same second-minute and with the same disk error as payment-service, the fault originates in the shared ledger-db, not in payment-service v6.0.0; payment-service is the reported victim.
